title: What ShopCoach is told about the inspection findings
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit' and 'Work orders - Create & Edit', on the build under test; ShopCoach is enabled and the shop has at least one labor type.
  2. A completed inspection with at least one Monitor/Not OK finding, including a per-axle finding with a note (seed a template with a checkbox and a per-axle field; flag and note them). Choose the target work order to reach the brief.
custom_steps:
1. Note for the tester: the exact brief sent to ShopCoach is internal and cannot be read from the screen — checking its wording is a developer/automated check. By hand, verify the brief did its job by reading the proposed lines it produced.
2. Build the lines and check every Monitor and Not OK finding produced at least one proposed line, and that a per-axle finding's line names its axle and measurement row so it can be traced back to the measurement.
3. Check no proposed line invents a part that was not in the inspection, and no passing (OK or N/A) finding became a line.
4. Check the proposed lines read as work for this asset (labor and parts), consistent with the recorded findings.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The brief sent to ShopCoach is composed from the inspection: for each Monitor and Not OK finding it includes the field label, its section, the measured value and its unit, the verdict and the technician's note.
  • A per-axle finding names its axle and its measurement row, so a proposed line can be traced back to the measurement that caused it.
  • The brief states what ShopCoach may not do: invent a part it was not given, turn a passing finding into a line, or leave a flagged finding unrepresented.
  • The brief follows the pattern of the existing asset-recommendation assistant — the asset's own data, then the material to reason about — with the inspection's flagged findings in place of that assistant's work-order history.
  • The brief states the situation before the findings: an inspection of an asset in a heavy-duty repair shop, questions authored in advance by an admin, answers recorded by a technician, and every finding sent already flagged.
  • The brief carries the schema of the answer it expects, so the format is shown rather than described.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-9404 (S15 — Draft the lines with ShopCoach); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S15; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S15-R1: “The system will compose the brief it sends to ShopCoach from the inspection itself. For each Monitor and Not OK finding it will include the field label, its section, the measured value and its unit, the verdict, and the technician's note”
  • S15-R2: “A per-axle finding will name its axle and its measurement row, so a proposed line can be traced back to the measurement that caused it”
  • S15-R3: “The brief will state what ShopCoach may not do: invent a part it was not given, turn a passing finding into a line, or leave a flagged finding unrepresented”
  • S15-R18: “The brief will follow the pattern of the ShopCoach assistant that already recommends work from an asset — the asset's own data, then the material to reason about — with the inspection's flagged findings in place of that assistant's work-order history”
  • S15-R19: “The brief will state the situation before the findings: an inspection of an asset in a heavy-duty repair shop, questions authored in advance by an admin, answers recorded by a technician, and every finding sent already flagged”
  • S15-R20: “The brief will carry the schema of the answer it expects, so the format is shown rather than described”

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
